title: feat(plugin-sharing)!: declared sharing rules, queues and assignment rules resolve on (package, name)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi99JCJQQzUUHvZbCS5kKcE7Y)_

Fixes #31675

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: follow-up #31735
Narrowing: (1) a bare name of a sharing rule, queue or assignment rule that two packages declare is refused, naming both (first-party: 0 names held twice); (2) a package item's bare reference whose only holder is an environment-authored item, D3 (a) (first-party: 0); (3) a package caller's bare reference whose one holder is a package outside its declared closure, per the epic seat's reading 6728487836 (first-party: 0). Sibling in the same release artifact: 0. The one package-written reference these reads carry is a declared sharing rule's queue recipient, and no first-party package declares a queue recipient or a queue. (4) The standing grants of a declared sharing rule name two packages hold are revoked by the boot orphan sweep, reported as that refusal (#31677 Q1 ruling A); reachable only through a sealed clash from before phase 1 (first-party: 0).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：共享插件里按名字读「声明的共享规则、队列、分配规则」的地方，全部改走 objectql 的同一个包寻址解析器。一个名字只有一个包声明时，答案和以前完全一样；两个包声明同名时，不再悄悄取第一个（`queuesOf` 原来取最后一个），而是拒绝并列出两个包。声明的共享规则把队列当接收方时，从规则所在的包去解析：本包的队列或它声明依赖的包的队列，范围外或只有环境项持有就拒绝并点名。
- 为什么改：专题 #31527 的子卡 E4（ADR-0150 D3/D4）。两个包同名时取哪个取决于注册顺序，授权和派单因此可能落到错误的包上，而且没有任何提示。
- 风险与回滚：只有「已安装两个包声明同名共享规则/队列/分配规则」的部署会看到变化：那个名字不再生效，日志 warn 一次，按名查询返回 409 列出两个包。第一方实测 0 个。组织自建的 `sys_queue`、`sys_sharing_rule`、`sys_assignment_rule` 行行为不变。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/package-scoped-declarations.ts`（唯一的入口，读 R 的解析器）；`ownership-queue-service.ts` 的 `resolve` / `declaredQueueNamed` / `activeDeclaredQueues`；`sharing-rule-service.ts` 的 `assertQueueRecipientReachable`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing exec vitest run src/package-scoped-declarations.test.ts`，预期 17 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

Every read in `plugin-sharing` that picks a declared sharing rule, queue or assignment rule by bare name now goes through one module, `package-scoped-declarations.ts`. That module reads objectql's `resolvePackageScopedName` (child R) and resolves nothing itself: no first-registered fallback, no pick.

- **The population is the listing.** The names asked about are the items `listItems(type)` lists, which hides a disabled package's items, as every one of these readers did before. One listed item of a name is that item, so there is nothing to choose. Two or more go to the resolver as a caller with no package. These reads are the platform enumerating its declarations and the Setup doors that switch or guard them, and none of them belongs to a package (ADR-0150 D3). A registry without the package-scoped slice (the kernel `metadata` service fallback on a registry-less host) gets no pick either: two holders listed means a refusal naming them.
- **Declared sharing rules** (`declared-sharing-rules.ts`): `list()` serves one rule per name through the module. The old one-rule-per-name skip kept the first holder silently, on the stated premise that the registry refuses a second holder, which is false for this uncovered type. A refused name serves nothing and is logged once at `warn`, naming both packages. Its grants carry the bare name, so serving either holder would grant on a guess; the grants it already has are revoked by the boot orphan sweep and reported as that refusal, naming both. New `lookup(name)` on the source; `SharingRuleService.declaredRuleNamed` reads it and throws `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, every candidate named) on a refusal. That covers the name guard on `sys_sharing_rule` writes (the name stays taken), `defineRule`, the activation door's lookup, and `getRule` / `resolveRules` by name (a refusal, never a misleading 404).
- **Queues** (`ownership-queue-service.ts`): `resolve` (so `resolveQueue`, `expandMembers`, `isMember`), `declaredQueueNamed` (the activation door's lookup), and `activeDeclaredQueues` (so `queuesOf`, `hasAnyQueue`, `queuesNaming`) go through the module. A refused name resolves nowhere for a `nobody` consumer, which denies. For a `refuse` consumer it rejects with the resolver's refusal, passed through unwrapped. It stays a declared name, so no `sys_queue` row may take it (`isDeclaredQueueName` is unchanged: any holder).
- **Assignment rules** (`assignment-rule-hooks.ts`): the `sys_assignment_rule` save guard asks the module. One holder gives the same message as before. Two holders still refuse, and the message now names both packages.
- **A declared rule's queue recipient** (`sharing-rule-service.ts`, `assertQueueRecipientReachable`): this is the one reference in these reads that a package writes, so it resolves from the rule's package P (ADR-0150 D3): P's own queue, else the unique holder in P's declared closure plus `sys`. A refusal (outside the closure, D3 (a), or ambiguous in the closure) throws, so each recompute keeps the rule's grants and warns, as for a failed read. A name no registry item holds passes through to an organization's `sys_queue` row, unchanged.
- Changeset: patch for `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, BREAKING (narrowing), ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

## Tests

New file `src/package-scoped-declarations.test.ts` (17 cases), built on the real `SchemaRegistry` (packages through `installPackage`, items under composite slots):

- `one holder` (3): sharing rule list and by-name, queue resolve, expand and `queuesOf`, and the assignment guard all answer as before.
- `two holders` (9): the resolver names both; the sharing rule is served by neither path and reported once; by-name gives 409 naming both; the name guard still refuses; the queue resolves nowhere and gives 409 under `refuse`; `queuesOf` serves neither; the door lookup gives 409 and the name stays declared; the assignment guard names both; the orphan sweep revokes the name's standing grants and reports them once as the refusal naming both, apart from a vanished rule's orphans.
- `listing without the slice` (1).
- `queue recipient from the rule's package` (4): outside closure refused; D3 (a) refused; a declared dependency's queue served; own queue served.

No existing test was edited. Package suite on head: Test Files 72 passed (72), Tests 1487 passed (1487).

## Acceptance notes

- **Caller package for queues.** The queue service's contract (`IOwnershipQueueService`, spec) has no caller-package argument, so after the P-side check it still resolves the name environment-wide. A name P's closure reaches once but an unrelated package also holds is therefore refused, where D3 alone would serve P's reach. That is stricter, never looser. Threading the caller through the contract is a spec change. Accepted as an interim by the epic seat (6729421618); carrier: #31734.
- **Organization-authored rows are not registry items.** `sys_queue`, `sys_sharing_rule` and `sys_assignment_rule` rows are read as before. D3 (a) applies only to environment-authored registry items (the bare slot).
- **The activation door** (runtime `catalog-activation.ts`, outside this card's surface) answers a thrown lookup with `503`, quoting the refusal, which names both packages. Carrier: G1 #31691 (the door's `409`); S1 owns the ledger's package column.
- **Grants of a refused sharing-rule name.** Under the maintainer's ruling on #31677 Q1 (A: a name two packages hold is refused and declared) a refused rule is served to nobody, so its standing grants must not keep answering. The boot orphan sweep revokes them, and reports it as a refusal, not an orphan: one `warn` per name naming every candidate package and saying the grants come back once the rule is addressed by package. Only a vanished rule's grants are counted in the sweep's orphan line. Reachable only through a sealed clash from before phase 1; first-party count 0.

## Verification

Head `b24fd3bca` (the Q2 change of the epic seat's revised ruling, merged with main).

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing test` (under `os-verify-lock`): 72 files / 1487 tests passed; new file 17/17. `typecheck` exit 0; `eslint --no-inline-config src` exit 0.
- `pnpm build` (whole workspace, under the lock): exit 0. A first attempt failed in `@object-ui/fields` (`Cannot find module '@objectstack/formula'`), a dependency main added that this worktree had not linked; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` then the build passed.
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: 72 derived, 72 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, every one exit 0.
- Dogfood, full battery on `b24fd3bca` under the lock: Test Files 440 passed, 3 skipped (443); Tests 3652 passed, 41 skipped (3693); VERDICT command-exit 0.
- CI on `b24fd3bca`: every check run success or skipped (50 runs).
- First-party counts (showcase): 2 declared sharing rules, 0 queues, 0 assignment rules. Names held twice: 0. D3 (a): 0. Outside the closure: 0. Sibling in the same release artifact: 0. Pre-phase-1 sealed clash: 0.

<details><summary>Step 0, main at b126c130: two packages declaring one name, every reader</summary>

Probe on the same fixture (ALPHA then BETA, each declaring sharing rule `emea_share`, queue `triage`, assignment rule `route_accounts`), source restored from `b126c130`:

| Reader | main | this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|
| declared sharing rules `list()` | ALPHA's rule only (first) | neither; one `warn` naming both |
| `declaredRuleNamed` (name guard, door lookup, `defineRule`) | ALPHA's rule | 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, both named |
| sharing name guard on insert | 409 (declared) | 409 (refusal naming both) |
| `resolveQueue` | ALPHA (first) | `null` |
| `expandMembers` | `["u_alpha"]` | `[]` |
| `expandMembers` under `refuse` | `["u_alpha"]` | 409, both named |
| `declaredQueueNamed` (activation door) | ALPHA | 409, both named |
| `queuesOf(u_alpha)` / `queuesOf(u_beta)` | `[]` / `["triage"]` (LAST holder's members) | `[]` / `[]` |
| assignment guard | refused, no holder named | refused, both named |
</details>

<details><summary>Ablation: four legs, each red, each restored (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs)</summary>

The tests import plugin-sharing source directly; objectql (dist) is not mutated. Each leg: anchor 1 to 0, blob changed, run red, restore proved by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- A1, the resolver's refusal answered as the first listed holder (`package-scoped-declarations.ts`): 7 red, every `two holders` refusal pin. The name-guard pin stays green, as a preservation pin should: the name is refused either way.
- A2, the listing refusal answered as the first holder: 1 red (`a listing that cannot be asked …`).
- A3, the P-side queue recipient check skipped: 2 red (outside closure; D3 (a)).
- A4, the orphan sweep's refusal report removed (`this.reportSweptRefusal(refusal)`): 1 red (the sweep pin).
</details>

<details><summary>ADR-0150's four readings</summary>

- (a) Phase-1 one-holder tests: no phase-1 file is touched (`bare-name-one-holder.ts`, its tests, the registry). The three types here are uncovered by phase 1, and their one-holder answers are pinned unchanged in the `one holder` block.
- (b) Bare-name behaviour for a name with one holder is unchanged on every read (`one holder` block), and no URL, MCP or SDK shape changes. The declared narrowings stand in for two holders, for a holder outside the rule package's closure, and for an environment-only holder.
- (c) No migration in this PR.
- (d) `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. No protocol change, so no ADR-0087 entry (changeset marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; `check-adr-0087-registration` exit 0).
</details>
